concepts.name: NPA Classification: Categories and Time Thresholds
key_dimensions: Distinction between Sub-standard, Doubtful, and Loss assets with exact time thresholds (90-day overdue norm)
Special mention accounts (SMA-0, SMA-1, SMA-2) as precursors to NPA — often confused with NPA itself
Out-of-order criteria for cash credit/overdraft accounts vs. overdue criteria for term loans
RBI's role in setting classification norms vs. banks' internal provisioning policies

concepts.name: Provisioning Norms for NPAs
key_dimensions: Differentiated provisioning rates: Sub-standard (15%), Doubtful-I/II/III (25%–100%), Loss assets (100%)
Secured vs. unsecured exposure provisioning differences — a common UPSC trap
Counter-cyclical provisioning buffer and its macroprudential significance
Impact of provisioning on bank profitability, capital adequacy, and credit growth

concepts.name: SARFAESI Act, 2002: Scope and Limitations
key_dimensions: Three mechanisms: Securitisation, Asset Reconstruction, Enforcement of Security Interest
Threshold conditions: loans above ₹1 lakh, security interest must be created — exclusions are a trap area
Assets excluded from SARFAESI: agricultural land, loans below threshold, no security interest cases
Borrower's right to appeal under DRT within 45 days — procedural trap in MCQs

concepts.name: Debt Recovery Tribunals (DRTs) and Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunals (DRATs)
key_dimensions: Established under RDDBFI Act 1993 — jurisdiction over banks and financial institutions only, not NBFCs (trap)
Minimum claim threshold: ₹20 lakh for DRT jurisdiction
DRT vs. DRAT hierarchy and appeal timelines (45 days to DRAT)
Overlap and interface with SARFAESI Act proceedings — which takes precedence

concepts.name: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016: Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP)
key_dimensions: Eligibility to trigger CIRP: Financial creditors, Operational creditors, Corporate debtor itself — thresholds differ
Minimum default threshold: ₹1 crore (raised from ₹1 lakh in 2020) — frequently tested
Strict timeline: 180 days + 90-day extension + Supreme Court's 330-day outer limit
Moratorium under Section 14 — what is included and what is excluded (critical trap area)

concepts.name: IBC: Committee of Creditors (CoC) and Voting Thresholds
key_dimensions: Composition: Only Financial Creditors — operational creditors excluded from voting (key UPSC trap)
Voting thresholds: 66% for approval of resolution plan, 75% for liquidation (asymmetry is tested)
Role of Resolution Professional (RP) vs. Interim Resolution Professional (IRP) — appointment and powers
Related party financial creditors: excluded from CoC voting — recent amendment trap

concepts.name: Financial Creditors vs. Operational Creditors under IBC
key_dimensions: Definitional distinction: financial debt (time value of money) vs. operational debt (goods/services)
Priority in liquidation waterfall: financial creditors rank above operational creditors
Operational creditors' limited rights: no CoC membership, can only trigger CIRP after 10-day demand notice
Homebuyers' classification as financial creditors — landmark amendment and judicial evolution

concepts.name: IBC Liquidation Waterfall (Priority of Claims)
key_dimensions: Statutory order: IBBI costs → workmen dues (24 months) → secured creditors → employee dues → unsecured creditors → government dues → equity
Government dues rank below unsecured financial creditors — counterintuitive and frequently tested
Workmen dues vs. secured creditor claims: partial priority and sharing mechanism
Distinction between liquidation value and going concern value in resolution planning

concepts.name: Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARCs): Structure and Functioning
key_dimensions: Regulated by RBI under SARFAESI Act; minimum Net Owned Fund requirements
Security Receipts (SRs) mechanism — how ARCs raise funds from Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs)
15:85 structure (ARC pays 15% cash, 85% in SRs) — recent RBI push to increase cash component to 15%
NARCL (National ARC) and India Debt Resolution Company Ltd (IDRCL) — bad bank model distinction

concepts.name: Bad Bank Model: NARCL and IDRCL
key_dimensions: NARCL acquires stressed assets; IDRCL manages and resolves them — two-entity structure rationale
Government guarantee of ₹30,600 crore on Security Receipts — contingent liability implication
Eligibility: fully provisioned assets above ₹500 crore — threshold is a trap
Comparison with earlier ARC model and why a new structure was needed (incentive alignment)

concepts.name: RBI's Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) Framework
key_dimensions: Three trigger indicators: Capital (CRAR), Asset Quality (Net NPA ratio), Profitability (RoA) — exact thresholds tested
Restrictions imposed: dividend distribution, branch expansion, management compensation — not a moratorium
PCA vs. moratorium under Section 45 of Banking Regulation Act — critical distinction
Recent extension of PCA to government-owned NBFCs and its implications

concepts.name: RBI's Revised Framework for Resolution of Stressed Assets (Post-February 2018 Circular)
key_dimensions: Supreme Court's April 2019 ruling striking down the original circular — grounds of ultra vires (Section 35AA)
New framework under June 2019 circular: 30-day review period, ICA signing, 180-day resolution timeline
Inter-Creditor Agreement (ICA) and majority lender (75% by value, 60% by number) decision binding on all
Divergence reporting requirement and additional provisioning for non-compliance

concepts.name: Wilful Defaulters: Definition, Consequences, and Related Controversies
key_dimensions: Four circumstances constituting wilful default: fund diversion, siphoning, asset disposal, refusal to pay despite capacity
Consequences: debarred from institutional finance, criminal proceedings, cannot be resolution applicant under IBC
Section 29A of IBC — ineligibility criteria for resolution applicants (promoters of NPA firms, wilful defaulters)
Controversy: balance between deterrence and genuine business failure; Supreme Court's interpretation of Section 29A

concepts.name: Section 29A of IBC: Ineligibility of Resolution Applicants
key_dimensions: Disqualifies: wilful defaulters, undischarged insolvents, convicted persons, connected persons of above categories
'Related party' and 'connected person' definitions — broad scope creates traps in MCQs
ArcelorMittal and Essar Steel cases — Supreme Court's interpretation of lookback period and NPA accounts
Tension between maximising resolution value and excluding promoters — policy debate angle

concepts.name: Twin Balance Sheet Problem and its Macroeconomic Implications
key_dimensions: Simultaneous stress on bank balance sheets (NPAs) and corporate balance sheets (over-leverage)
Transmission mechanism: credit crunch → investment slowdown → GDP deceleration
India-specific context: infrastructure sector concentration of NPAs post-2008 lending boom
4R strategy (Recognition, Resolution, Recapitalisation, Reform) — each element's policy instrument

concepts.name: Bank Recapitalisation: Instruments and Fiscal Implications
key_dimensions: Recap bonds mechanism: government issues bonds to banks, banks subscribe — no immediate cash outflow but increases fiscal deficit over time
Distinction between budgetary recapitalisation, recap bonds, and market-raising — fiscal impact differs
Indradhanush framework (2015) — 7-element reform package beyond just capital infusion
Basel III capital adequacy requirements as the driver for recapitalisation urgency

concepts.name: One-Time Settlement (OTS) and Compromise Settlement Schemes
key_dimensions: RBI's June 2023 circular allowing compromise settlements even for wilful defaulters — controversy and rationale
Difference between OTS (bank-borrower negotiation) and resolution under IBC (court-supervised)
Moral hazard concerns: incentivising strategic default vs. pragmatic recovery of stressed assets
Cooling-off period and debarment provisions post-settlement to address moral hazard

concepts.name: Securitisation of Assets: Process and Regulatory Framework
key_dimensions: SPV (Special Purpose Vehicle) structure: true sale concept, bankruptcy remoteness
Pass-through certificates (PTCs) vs. pay-through certificates — cash flow distribution difference
Minimum Retention Requirement (MRR) and Minimum Holding Period (MHP) — RBI norms to prevent originate-to-distribute moral hazard
Role of credit enhancement and rating in securitisation — linkage to 2008 global financial crisis lessons

concepts.name: IBBI (Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India): Powers and Jurisdiction
key_dimensions: Regulatory oversight over IPs (Insolvency Professionals), IPAs, and Information Utilities
Quasi-judicial powers: investigation, inspection, penalty — distinction from NCLT's adjudicatory role
NCLT as adjudicating authority for corporates vs. DRT for individuals and partnership firms — jurisdictional trap
IBBI's role in cross-border insolvency framework development (Model Law adoption status)

concepts.name: Pre-packaged Insolvency Resolution Process (PIRP) for MSMEs
key_dimensions: Introduced in 2021 — key difference from CIRP: debtor-in-possession model vs. creditor-in-control
Eligibility: only MSMEs with default up to ₹1 crore; promoter retains management during process
Base resolution plan submitted by debtor upfront — Swiss challenge mechanism if CoC rejects it
Faster timeline (120 days vs. 330 days) and lower costs — rationale for separate MSME framework
